purpose: Metric definitions, limitations and plotting instructions for a rigorous teaching tutorial.
global_rules: All company outcomes below are reported by suppliers or named customers in supplier-hosted stories; none is an independent causal study.
A missing sample size, uncertainty estimate or metric definition must remain unknown.
Do not place heterogeneous company metrics on a common performance leaderboard.
Bounds, approximations and projections must remain visibly marked.

sources.location: 2025 pilot account; scale and advisory architecture
CAISO section, paragraphs beginning 'Start with the scale' and 'The results CAISO reported'

cases.status: Customer described a pilot in 2025; supplier's 2026 field report describes production outage-review assistance.

metrics.definition: Nightly automated analysis of next-day outage requests
metrics.observation_period: Nightly; number of observed nights not disclosed
metrics.includes: Modeling/market-impact checks, historical comparison, keyword analysis
metrics.excludes_or_unknown: Human review time; request complexity; failures/retries; hardware/concurrency; per-request latency; tail percentiles

safe_derivation.assumptions: Use only as an arithmetic lower bound on reported batch throughput; not independent measurement.

metrics.definition: RC West contextual workload, not the timed AI batch

analyst_effort.unit: analyst-hours across teams per outage day

cannot_infer: Do not divide 40 analyst-hours by 8 machine minutes: task scopes and time types differ.
No measured hours saved, false-negative rate, per-request p95 or reliability gain is supplied.
Do not combine RC West workload with the narrower CAISO balancing-area chart as one population.
cases.recommended_plot: Annotate a nightly batch with ≥500 requests and <8 min; optionally show throughput >62.5 requests/min as a labeled derived lower bound.

sources.location: Headline results and 'Transforming safety and efficiency'

cases.status: Operational safety-audit agents with human examination retained.

metrics.definition: Audit results/report turnaround; precise start/end boundary not specified

evaluation_cohort.caveat: Not a disclosed paired sample or metric-specific denominator

annual_volume.unit: audits/year; internal and external in Google account

metrics.cannot_infer: 100 employee-hours is not 14 calendar days of continuous labor; no post-agent person-hour value is given.

metrics.reason: No defensible accuracy axis or absolute score can be reconstructed.

metrics.claim_type: Capacity statement ('can double'), not a disclosed completed-year production count
metrics.human_work: Customer says agents handle half the workload; remaining human examination stays
metrics.cannot_infer: Do not equate workload share with a measured 50% reduction in employee-hours.

source_disagreement.assessment: Both narratives describe approximately two weeks to one hour, but their percentage headlines differ. Use native times and do not silently select a derived speedup.

cannot_infer: No exact speedup ratio without defining the day and process boundary.
No error-free audit guarantee or measured safety improvement.
No annual labor savings by multiplying 1,500, 100 hours and the cost percentage.
cases.recommended_plot: Show native reported times '14 days → ~1 hour' with scope note. A cost index of 100→1 is a derived display of the reported 99% reduction, with the unspecified cost boundary prominent.

sources.location: Program description and 'What you can do'

cases.status: Duke engineers already using specialized AWS agents in planning when program launched.

metrics.cannot_infer: No numeric speedup ratio, per-study end-to-end time or engineering-headcount reduction.

metrics.definition: Program study-task speed relative to manual analysis
metrics.attribution: AWS program-level claim, not specifically a Duke result

cannot_infer: The 4× and 92% claims measure different quantities and need not be from the same task.
Do not assign those two program maxima to Duke or multiply them.
Study agents coordinate existing deterministic simulation software; no measured interconnection-queue or grid-reliability outcome is supplied.
cases.recommended_plot: Use a native-unit annotated comparison '2 weeks of manual preparation → hours (not specified)' for Duke. Keep generic program maxima visually separate.

cases.status: Pipeline-record agent used by engineers; Canadian-headquartered North American operator.

metrics.reason: Reported range is not a confidence interval; accuracy unit and sample are unknown.

metrics.definition: Expected avoided maintenance capital expenditure, PIPER and SCOUT combined
metrics.cannot_infer: Not realized annual savings, revenue, or a cost result attributable to PIPER alone.

cannot_infer: Accuracy on tested documents ≤120 pages does not establish accuracy on the >1,000-page packages mentioned as a challenge.
More than 100 users does not establish a sample of 100 timing or accuracy tests.
No physical maintenance, pipeline safety or electric-grid reliability effect was measured in the public account.
cases.recommended_plot: Within-case review-time index 100→15, explicitly derived from the reported 85% reduction. Preserve unknown absolute duration and review scope; do not rank it against AES or Duke.

operator_evidence.title: An Analysis of Grid Operators
operator_evidence.population: 20 electric-grid power control-room operators; recruitment and representativeness not disclosed

metric.statistic: reported average share of tasks requiring completion in under 30 minutes
metric.task_scope: Tasks performed or supported by operators

operator_evidence.interpretation: Small-sample survey/self-report context, not national prevalence or observed task timing.
cannot_infer: Not 61% of operators; do not calculate 12.2 respondents.
Not a sample of 75 tasks or 1,500 independent observations.
No binomial confidence interval is justified from N=20 and 61%.
operator_evidence.safe_slide_label: A PNNL survey of 20 operators reported an average 61% of tasks requiring completion within 30 minutes.
